claim: The General Assembly convenes every year on the second Tuesday of January
quote: shall convene at the State Capitol Building in the City of Columbia on the second Tuesday of January of each year

claim: The regular session adjourns sine die by 5 p.m. on the second Thursday in May unless extended
quote: shall adjourn sine die each year not later than five o'clock p.m. on the second Thursday in May

claim: The presiding officers may call the houses back until the end of June to finish the budget
quote: may call their respective bodies into session at any time after the date of sine die adjournment and until the last day in June

claim: A bill not returned by the governor within five days, Sundays excepted, becomes law; if adjournment prevents return, within two days after the next meeting
quote: within five days after it shall have been presented to him, Sundays excepted

claim: If adjournment prevents return, the bill becomes law unless returned within two days after the next meeting
quote: unless returned within two days after the next meeting

claim: General elections for state and county officers are on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years
quote: shall be held on the first Tuesday following the first Monday in November in each even-numbered year

claim: County supervisors, superintendents of education, sheriffs, coroners and clerks of court are elected every four years, counting from 1960
quote: held in each county at every alternate general election, reckoning from the year 1960

claim: Probate judges are elected every four years, counting from 1958
quote: The probate judge in every county shall be elected at every alternate general election, reckoning from the year 1958

claim: County council members are elected at the general election for two- or four-year terms set by the General Assembly
quote: shall be elected in the general election for terms of two years or four years as the General Assembly may determine for each county

claim: Council members are elected from single-member districts unless otherwise determined
quote: Council members must be elected from defined single-member election districts unless otherwise determined

claim: Each county elects a clerk of court, sheriff and coroner for four years; each judicial circuit elects a solicitor
quote: There shall be elected in each county by the electors thereof a clerk of the circuit court, a sheriff, and a coroner; and in each judicial circuit a solicitor shall be elected by the electors thereof

claim: From 1 January 2027, municipal general elections are held in odd-numbered years, in April or November
quote: The time for general elections within a municipality must be established in odd-numbered years as follows

claim: The April option is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in April
quote: on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in April; or

claim: A municipality that votes in November of odd years cannot change
quote: then the municipal governing body must not establish a different time for its general elections

claim: A municipality that failed to choose defaults to November of odd years
quote: then the time for the general elections within that municipality is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in odd-numbered years unless subsection (E) applies

claim: A municipality whose last elections were in April or November of an even year may keep that even-year date
quote: then the municipality may retain the first Tuesday after the first Monday in April in even-numbered years

claim: Terms are adjusted in the transition so current terms end at the new odd-year dates
quote: Notwithstanding Section 5-15-40, if the unexpired four-year term of a mayor or member of council began following a general election held

claim: Until 1 January 2027 a municipality sets its election time by ordinance
quote: Each municipal governing body may by ordinance establish municipal ward lines and the time for general and special elections within the municipality

claim: Mayor and council serve two- or four-year terms; four-year terms are staggered unless an ordinance says otherwise
quote: The mayor and councilmen of each municipality shall be elected for terms of two or four years

claim: Two-year terms are not staggered
quote: Two-year terms shall not be staggered

claim: A party nominates by primary, convention, or petition candidates qualify by petition
quote: may be by political party primary, by political party convention, or by petition

claim: A candidate defeated in a party primary or convention cannot appear on the general election ballot for that office
quote: a person who was defeated as a candidate for nomination to an office in a party primary or party convention must not have his name placed on the ballot for the ensuing general or special election

claim: Party primaries are held on the second Tuesday in June of general election years, with runoffs two weeks later
quote: on the second Tuesday in June of each general election year, and a second and third primary each two weeks successively thereafter, if necessary

claim: State-run June primaries include all school boards and special purpose district offices where parties nominate
quote: countywide and less than countywide offices, specifically including, but not limited to, all school boards and school trustees

claim: No person may vote in more than one party primary on the same day
quote: No person shall be entitled to vote in more than one party primary election held the same day

claim: A first primary needs a majority to nominate
quote: No candidate shall be declared nominated in a first primary election unless he received a majority of the votes cast for the office

claim: The second primary is between the top two, two weeks later, and the leader wins
quote: A second primary, when necessary, must be held two weeks after the first

claim: In the second primary the candidate with the most votes is nominated even without a majority
quote: must be declared the nominee for the office whether or not he has received a majority of the votes cast for that office

claim: The general election ballot groups candidates under party names, with columns for petition candidates
quote: with a column or columns added in case of nomination by petition

claim: Each municipality adopts by ordinance one of three methods for nonpartisan elections
quote: shall adopt by ordinance one of the following alternative methods of nominating candidates for and determining the results of its nonpartisan elections

claim: From 2027, partisan municipal nominations are allowed only in municipalities under 39,000 people
quote: only in municipalities with populations under thirty-nine thousand according to the most recent official United States census

claim: A municipality over 39,000 with partisan nominations must adopt a nonpartisan method by 1 April 2027 or default to plurality
citation: 2026 S.C. Acts, editor's note to S.C. Code § 5-15-60
quote: must, by April 1, 2027, adopt by ordinance a method of nominating candidates prescribed in Section 5-15-61, 5-15-62, or 5-15-63

claim: A municipality that holds partisan elections pays for its municipal primary
quote: any municipality which elects to hold partisan elections for municipal offices must pay all costs and expenses associated with the conduct of a municipal primary election

claim: Under the nonpartisan plurality method the candidate with the most votes wins
quote: the candidate who receives the highest number of votes shall be declared elected

claim: Under the election-and-runoff method a majority is needed, with a runoff two weeks later
quote: a second election shall be conducted two weeks later between the two candidates receiving the largest number of votes in the first election who do not withdraw

claim: The third method is a nonpartisan primary followed by a general election
quote: The nonpartisan primary election and general election method prescribed in Section 5-15-63

claim: Petition candidates file with the county board of voter registration and elections for county offices and with the municipal clerk for municipal offices
quote: with the county board of voter registration and elections in the case of countywide or less than countywide offices with the exception of municipal offices; with the clerk of a municipality in case of a municipal office

claim: Petitions must be signed by qualified registered electors of the office's area
quote: qualified registered electors of the geographical area of the office for which he offers as a candidate

claim: No more than 46 counties may exist
quote: counties shall exist at any time, but the General Assembly may provide for a lesser number

claim: The General Assembly sets county structure by general law, with no more than five forms, and may pass no law for a specific county
quote: No laws for a specific county shall be enacted and no county shall be exempted from the general laws

claim: The five county forms are council, council-supervisor, council-administrator, council-manager and board of commissioners
quote: The alternate forms of government which may be adopted pursuant to Section 4-9-10 shall be one of the following

claim: The council-administrator form council has 3 to 12 members
quote: shall consist of not less than three nor more than twelve members who are qualified electors of the county

claim: Under the council-supervisor form the supervisor is elected at large, chairs the council and votes only to break ties
quote: The supervisor shall serve as chairman and vote only to break tie votes

claim: The council picks its chair unless the chair is elected as a separate office
quote: The council shall select one of its members as chairman, except where the chairman is elected as a separate office

claim: County powers are liberally construed
quote: The powers of a county must be liberally construed in favor of the county

claim: Home rule laws cannot set aside general law on election and suffrage qualifications
quote: election and suffrage qualifications

claim: A municipality is a city or town with a certificate of incorporation, or a township created by act
quote: "Municipality" means a city or town issued a certificate of incorporation, or township created by act of the General Assembly

claim: Municipal forms: mayor-council, council, council-manager, chosen by ordinance
quote: the mayor-council form provided for in Chapter 9

claim: The council-manager form is one of the three
quote: the council-manager form provided for in Chapter 13

claim: No more than five municipal forms; structure set by general law
quote: that not more than five alternative forms of government shall be authorized

claim: No law may be enacted for a specific municipality
quote: No laws for a specific municipality shall be enacted

claim: Each municipality chooses by ordinance how council is elected (at large, wards, or a mix); the mayor is always elected at large
quote: Regardless of the form adopted by the municipality, the mayor shall be elected at large

claim: Council or voters by petition can call a referendum to change council size or method of election
quote: to change the number of council members to a number authorized by the form of government under which the municipality is then operating or to change the method of election of council members

claim: From 2027 elections in towns under 10,000 are run by the county election board
quote: Elections for municipalities with a population of less than ten thousand, according to the most recent official United States census, must be conducted and certified by the county boards of voter registration and elections

claim: Default school trustee boards are three appointed members for three years, unless a law provides otherwise
quote: Unless it be specially provided otherwise by law, the boards of school trustees in this State shall be composed of three members

claim: Public service district commissioners can be elected at the general election, nominated by petition
quote: petitions to nominate candidates elected in the general election to serve as commissioners of public service districts
